plan: This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and my exit point is determined by my own sealed bid. Since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding my true value is a weakly dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit without risk of overpaying, since I never pay more than my value if I win, and bidding higher/lower than my value doesn't help since the price I pay depends only on others' bids.

This auction structure mirrors a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, not their own. In such mechanisms, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy - bidding higher risks overpaying if I win, and bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities where the second-highest bid is between my true value and my lower bid. Since my value is $44, I should bid exactly $44 to maximize expected profit.

This mechanism is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and my bid only determines when I exit. Bidding my true value ($43) is the dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids, since I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid and pay exactly that amount, ensuring non-negative profit whenever I win.
